text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High rate of GPU OOMs during prefill on cluster us-west-2-runtime-3. Multiple containers restarted in last 3m. Auto-escalating to pager.
oncall-jen: saw it. getting logs now. looks like long multipart uploads + inline base64 are expanding token counts massively.
oncall-jen: quick snapshot: ~14 restarts across 6 pods, node group gpu-preempt-3,OOM at prefill stage (before generation). stack: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory when allocating 4.2 GiB (prefill)
  at /srv/runtime/infer.cpp:line 132
  kvcache alloc fail -> container restart
```
sre-omar: thanks jen. can we triage whether this is 1 noisy customer or broad traffic?
oncall-jen: initial grep of request headers shows many `content-type: multipart/form-data` and a few requests with huge embedded `data:` URIs.
cs-maya: heads up — two paying customers (acme-inc, finlytics) opened tickets about partial responses 2m ago. may be related.
infra-lee: recommendation: cordon nodes hosting the worst pods to stop restarts and move traffic. `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-42` and scale down daemonset on that node while we patch.
oncall-jen: running cordon now. also turning on request-size limiter at the ingress router to 1MB as emergency short-term.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by oncall-jen: routing/proxy -> limit-prefill-size v1.0.1 (canary 10%).
oncall-jen: canary looks okay for 1m, no new OOMs on canary pods. rolling to 100%.
sre-omar: good. also enable fallback to cpu-runtime for oversized-prefill requests so they don't take GPU memory. config snippet: 
```yaml
routing:
  rule: if request.prefill_bytes > 1_000_000 -> backend: cpu-fallback
```
(I'll open PR to make that default for now.)
infra-lee: after cordon I'll restart the restart-looping pods gracefully to clear corrupted KV caches: `kubectl delete pod pod-abc --grace-period=30` on affected nodes.
oncall-jen: restarted pods, cordon still in place, CPU fallback routing live. no new OOM alerts in last 90s. marking mitigation in progress.
cs-maya: drafting customer update: "We experienced transient failures for generation requests containing large attachments/inline-encoded content. We applied a mitigation and are routing oversized prefill requests to a CPU fallback. If you see partial responses, please reply and we'll investigate." want to add ETA for fix.
product-igor: what's long-term plan? we need detection + soft-failure before GPU allocation. also add explicit max-prefill-tokens and a clear 413 response.
sre-omar: agree. follow-ups: 1) add pre-allocate check that rejects prefill if estimated token > N, 2) hard-limit input expansion for data URIs, 3) add quick evict path for kvcache on prefill failures to avoid restarts.
oncall-jen: created incident ticket #INC-2026-118 with notes and actions.
oncall-jen: handing off to next oncall @oncall-sam for overnight watch. leaving cordon in place and cpu-fallback enabled. oncall-sam please verify autoscaler doesn't reschedule to cordoned nodes.
oncall-sam: ack, taking over. I'll run a sweep and check for any remaining pod restarts. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy complete: limit-prefill-size v1.0.1 -> stable.
cs-maya: sending customer note now. will follow up if they report data loss.
product-igor: add to roadmap: "prefill safety checks" and UX: clearer 413 messages when we reject oversized payloads.
sre-omar: postmortem owners: omar (technical), jen (ops), maya (customer comms), igor (product). timeline to draft: 24h.
oncall-sam: quick check in — stack traces still show occasional mem spike on node gpu-node-48 but no restarts. I'll uncordon node-42 once autoscaler confirms capacity and then monitor.
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied (prefill limiter + cpu fallback), cordon applied, affected customers notified. Severity: degraded. Next update in 30m or on significant change.
